subject: Volume-trigger tiers and reseller split — clarification request (AWS private offer)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimbushealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marketplace-support@amazonaws.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Volume-trigger tiers & reseller split for AWS private offer

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. Procurement is starting the paperwork and we have one outstanding question about how rebates / trigger tiers interact with the reseller margin on the AWS private offer. The draft PO is attached. Two specific asks: 

1) Our reseller (CloudWise) needs a predictable 12% net margin. If we layer a volume-triggered rebate (e.g., 10% rebate once usage > $250k/mo) that flows as a credit on the Marketplace invoice, will that reduce the reseller net below their 12% target, or can the rebate be applied upstream without impacting the reseller pass-through?

2) We also want to understand cadence: is the rebate applied monthly as a negative line item on the AWS invoice, or do you issue a separate credit (Redwood -> Nimbus) after reconciling usage? That changes revenue recognition and our payment timing.

Can you confirm how Redwood typically models the reseller split for private offers with usage-triggered rebates? If there's a recommended contract language to preserve the reseller net, please share.

Attached: Nimbus_PO_v1.pdf (draft PO), sku_mapping_olga.xlsx (requested SKU list).

Appreciate a quick confirmation — procurement hopes to finalize by 12/20.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Director, Procurement
Nimbus Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Volume-trigger tiers & reseller split for AWS private offer

Ben / Naomi — forwarding Tom's note from Nimbus (attached). They want a clean way to preserve a 12% reseller net when a usage-triggered rebate kicks in. PO attached.

Quick thoughts: we need to confirm AWS Marketplace invoice behavior (does the rebate show as a negative line on the Marketplace invoice or as a separate settlement?). Also need to choose between two operational approaches:

A) Marketplace-applied rebate: simplest for Nimbus (rebate appears on AWS invoice). Problem — reseller pass-through may be reduced unless we implement a backstop payment (Redwood pays reseller the difference). That requires us to make an extra settlement to CloudWise monthly.

B) Redwood-managed rebate: Redwood issues an off-invoice credit or a paid rebate to Nimbus after usage reconciliation, leaving Marketplace invoice amounts intact for reseller pass-through. Simpler for reseller margin but heavier on our accounting/ops.

I can ask AWS marketplace support about technical invoice semantics, but need your preference on which approach we can operationalize (and cost to Redwood). Can we model both options and offer Nimbus the choice?

If we do option A, what's the minimum uplift we need to hold on the PO so that reseller still nets 12% after rebates? If we do option B, we should propose language that spells out "Redwood rebate paid to Customer; reseller margin guaranteed at 12% of list invoice".

Please reply with a quick estimate for the channel uplift/waterfall so I can respond to Tom by EOD Friday.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Channel Pricing & Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Volume-trigger tiers & reseller split for AWS private offer

Olga — quick calc below, talking points for Nimbus: 

Option A (Marketplace rebate applied on AWS invoice):
- If list price L is invoiced on AWS, rebate R (10%) appears as negative line. Reseller receives L - R as basis. To preserve reseller 12% net, Redwood needs to top-up the reseller each month by amount = 0.12*(L) - 0.12*(L - R) = 0.12*R. So top-up = 0.12 * rebate_amount.
- Operationally: we'd net rebate to customer on AWS invoice; then Redwood sends monthly supplemental payment to CloudWise equal to reseller shortfall. That is predictable but requires monthly settlement.

Option B (Redwood-managed rebate off-invoice):
- AWS invoice stays at L, reseller pass-through preserved automatically. Redwood pays rebate to Nimbus separately. Easier for reseller but we carry the cash flow to Redwood.

Recommendation: offer both, default to B for customers that care about channel predictability. For Nimbus, propose Option B with a 30-day reconciliation window; if they insist on marketplace-invoice rebate, propose we implement a monthly top-up to CloudWise (Ben/Finance to confirm exact payment workflow).

Financial ask for leadership: estimated monthly cash out (if Option B chosen) = rebate_amount (10% of usage above trigger) less the timing delta; shortfall to reseller under A = 12% * rebate_amount (this is what we'd pay on top of the rebate flow).

I'll sync with Finance early week to confirm settlement cadence and required paperwork.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Volume-trigger tiers & reseller split for AWS private offer

Tom — thanks for the note and the PO. Quick summary and proposal so procurement can close by 12/20: 

Summary:
- Two viable operational approaches: (A) marketplace-applied rebate on AWS invoice; or (B) Redwood-managed off-invoice rebate paid to Nimbus.
- Reseller impact: marketplace-applied rebates reduce the invoice basis for CloudWise. To guarantee CloudWise a 12% net margin under option A, Redwood would perform a monthly top-up payment equal to 12% of the rebate amount (i.e., 12% * rebate). That preserves CloudWise net but adds a Redwood settlement step.
- Under option B, AWS invoice remains at list and CloudWise receives full pass-through. Redwood issues the rebate to Nimbus separately after monthly reconciliation. This preserves reseller margin without supplemental payments to CloudWise but requires Redwood to manage the rebate payment to Nimbus.

Our recommended default: Option B (Redwood-managed rebate). It minimizes changes to reseller cash flow and avoids confusing negative lines on Marketplace invoices. Operational details: 30-day reconciliation window after month-end; Redwood issues rebate by ACH within 10 business days of reconciliation. We will include contract language: "Redwood will pay Customer rebate amounts described in Schedule A. Redwood will ensure that reseller CloudWise receives a minimum net margin of 12% of the list invoice amount; any shortfall resulting from marketplace invoice credits will be remedied by Redwood via a monthly supplemental payment to the reseller."

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Nimbus is comfortable with Option B and the proposed timing (30-day reconciliation, ACH within 10 business days).
2) If Nimbus insists on marketplace-applied credits, we'll prepare a short supplemental agreement describing the monthly top-up to CloudWise (we'll share the draft within 48 hours).
3) I've looped in AWS Marketplace support to confirm technical invoice treatment — they should reply to the cc with any constraints.

If you want a short call to finalize language, Ben and Naomi are available Mon 12/21 morning PST.

Regards,
Olga
